_about: Solitude voice script. Every voiced line in the game. tools/voice/generate.py turns it into assets/audio/voice/*.wav (generated with Tom's NoorVox, then run through voice_fx.py) plus voice_lines.json, which the game reads. Captions are the text without the [tags]. Voices are Tom's designed NoorVox voices (no cloned people). Seeds make every take reproducible. Hanna's voice: NoorVox 'voices design --name Hanna --language english --description "A Polish woman in her late thirties, a deep-sea station engineer. Low, slightly hoarse and tired from bad air, with a dry sense of humour; she speaks quietly and close to the microphone, warm but worn out."' (design seed 1722989800).

lines.text: Haldane, Haldane. Holed aft, settling. Three aboard. [sigh] Nadia is hurt. If anyone hears this...
Day one. Loaded at the shelf. Stores for three stations, mail, and a crate of real coffee somebody bribed us for.
Day three. Nadia says the current's taking us east of the lane. Correcting.
Day three. Something hit the stern. Not a rock. [sniff] Rocks don't come back.
Day three. Holed aft. We're settling. Bram has the pinger running. We're fine. We're fine. Someone will come down the lane.
Meridian Bell to any station. We are on the bottom. Power is failing. Please acknowledge. [cough] Please... acknowledge.
Day twelve. The lane beacons are gone. All of them, one after the other, like someone walked the line turning them off.
Day thirteen. Sonar shows a ridge where the chart says flat. The ridge moved while we watched.
Day thirteen. We went dark. Engines off, lights off. It still found us.
Day fourteen. Air for two days. Kofi is writing letters. I told him there is no mail down here. He knows.
This is the Okonkwo. Grounded, no propulsion, crew of two. [groan] We have food. We have air. We need a tow.
Day five. The silt came down the slope like a wall. We couldn't see the bow from the bridge.
Day five. When it cleared we were somewhere else. The compass agrees with nothing.
Day six. Ilse heard tapping on the hull. Three taps, then three more. I said it was the cold. It's not the cold.
Day eight. Ilse went out to look. The tether came back. I'm keeping the pinger on for her.
Patience calling. Patience calling. [fear] We are taking water, and the pumps have stopped. Is anyone there?
Day two. Captain's log, Patience. A good run so far. Lena caught a ray in the lights and named it Gerald.
Day four. Gerald came back. Gerald brought friends. They follow the floodlights. All of them.
Day four. Something bigger followed Gerald. The lights went out on their own.
Day five. It's very dark. I'm not turning them back on.
Grey Heron. Lost steering, lost the lane. [clear throat] Two aboard, both fine. Pinger's on. We'll wait.
Day one. Old boat, good engine. Marek says she's older than both of us put together.
Day nine. Engine's knocking. Marek says she's just tired. We greased her twice.
Day ten. Seals weeping in the quarters. We should have turned back at the last station.
Day eleven. She stopped. Just stopped, like she'd had enough. I patted the wall. Stupid. Marek did it too.
Capsule two, two aboard. Air for... [cough] If you're the relief sub, we can hear you. We can hear you.
We left the station when the lights went the wrong colour. Tomas says we did the right thing.
Hour nine. Air is fine. Pinger is fine. Something circled us twice and left.
[whispering] Hour thirty-one. Tomas is asleep. I keep hearing counting through the hull. I've started counting back.
Hour forty. I've stopped.
Capsule four. One aboard. [sigh] I'm alright. I'm alright. Take your time.
I was the last one off the station. I closed the doors behind me. I don't know why. Habit.
Hour six. Something is walking on the seabed outside. Walking. Down here.
Hour twenty. It's stopped right next to the hatch.
[whispering] Hour twenty-one. It's knocking.
Escape capsule one. Three aboard. The children are fine. Please hurry. Please.
Hour one. The kids think it's an adventure. I told them we're a submarine now.
Hour twelve. We sang every song we know. Twice.
Hour twenty. They're asleep. The air smells like pennies.
Hour twenty-six. I can hear a motor. Something big, coming down the slope. It's slowing. [gasp] It's slowing for us.
Capsule three. [gasp] Can anyone... the hatch won't... just come. Please come.
We saw the station from the window as we left. The lights were all on. Every light.
Hour two. The lights were on in the core room. Nobody was in the core room.
Hour ten. The pinger is louder than it should be. Or something is answering it.
[whispering] Hour eleven. The hatch. Something is working the hatch from outside.
Survey drone. Fault. Awaiting recovery. Survey drone. Fault. Awaiting recovery.
Survey log, automatic. Transect complete. Bathymetry uploaded.
Anomalous return at the end of the line. Large. Warm. Moving against the current.
Collision. Pressure housing compromised. Entering low power mode. Awaiting recovery.
Survey drone. Battery critical. Please collect. Please collect.
Survey log, automatic. Water sample taken. Temperature rising with depth.
Sample contains structured particles. Classification failed. Classification failed.
Unit is being moved. Unit is being moved. Unit is...
[sigh] Still here.
Heading.
Depth.
Metres.
We're fine. Someone will come down the lane.
Zero.
One.
Two.
Three.
Four.
Five.
Six.
Seven.
Eight.
Nine.
[clear throat] Is that... is that a boat? I can hear an engine through the floor. If someone's there, ping twice. Please. Twice.
It's me again. I heard you go past. If you can hear me, ping twice. I won't ask a third time. [sigh] I will, actually.
[gasp] Two. That was two. Okay. Okay. My name's Hanna. Hanna Kowal. I'm an engineer, on a station not far from you. I'm sending you its beacon now.
I need air. My scrubber's dying. Two lattice crystals and a power cell, if you can spare them. There's a supply lock by the airlock. Use that. Don't come any further in.
That's you? That's really you. [sniff] Put it in the lock. Don't open the inner door. Please. It isn't safe in here.
[sigh] Oh, that's air. That's real air. Thank you, boat. I don't know your name. I'm going to call you boat.
Listen. I've been listening to the counting for months. Check your holo table. There's a station out there with its core still running. They didn't all go quiet.
Can I ask you something? My sister was on a supply boat. The Haldane. It never came. I've put its last position on your beacons. If you ever get there, I'd like to know.
[crying] Nadia was hurt? She never said she was hurt. She always... [sniff] Thank you. I needed to know. I needed to stop waiting.
There's an ascent capsule here. Old, but it holds pressure. It needs a full cell to make the surface. One more power cell, boat. Then I can go up.
It's charging. [laugh] It's actually charging. If the surface is still there, I'll tell them about you. A boat that pings twice. Goodbye, boat.
Boat? It's getting thin in here. If you're coming, come soon.
[whispering] I've started counting. It helps. One. Two. Three.
Still here.
[chuckle] Hello, boat.
